content.title: About
content.content: Luncheon meat (also known as canned meat) is a ready‑to‑eat meat product made from beef, pork or a mixture of both, seasoned with salt, spices and stabilizers. It is packed in a sealed can and can be stored at room temperature for extended periods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first canned meat recipes appeared in the United States in the early 20th century.
The term “luncheon meat” originated because the product was often served during lunch breaks.
Canned meat is popular for camping, military rations and emergency supplies.
Nitrites are commonly added to give the characteristic pink colour and to extend shelf life.
In different countries the product is known by various names: “spam”, “canned meat”, “meat loaf”.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Luncheon meat provides about 12–15 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from the meat helps form hemoglobin and prevents anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product supplies thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which are essential for metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Its high fat and protein content offers a quick source of energy.

items.title: Long shelf life
items.content: Sealed cans allow storage without refrigeration for several years.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Large amounts of salt can raise blood pressure; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Nitrites and preservatives
items.content: Some additives may cause allergic reactions or increase the risk of carcinogen formation with long‑term use.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: High levels of saturated fat may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A minority of individuals may be allergic to beef or pork.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The meat can be eaten straight from the can, sliced for sandwiches, added to salads, soups or stir‑fries. It is often warmed in a pan or microwave before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, store the remaining meat in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 5 days.
